note: Retired legends. Available for comebacks, commentary and the Hall of Fame.

fighters.bio: One more fight. Always one more fight. Fifty years old and still insists he's 'feeling 25'.
The most polite champion in history. Retired at the top and is 'definitely, absolutely not' coming back. (He might be coming back.)
Undefeated for a decade in an era before anyone kept track. Wears a sweater that has its own legend.
Mohawk, tattoo on the head, and an overhand right that defined an era. Comebacks have not gone well.
Won a title in his forties and acted in movies with explosions. Still does dirty boxing on unsuspecting gym members.

fighters.nick: The Huntington Beach Bad Boy (Now Mayor-ish)
fighters.bio: Digs an imaginary grave after every win. Has opinions about everything, most of them loud.
Pro wrestling superstar who walked into a cage and became champion. Lives on a farm, hates press, loves money.
Black belt in record time, champion in two divisions, and the most famous blood-licking celebration in history. Kept fighting long past the point anyone wanted him to.
Slammed people for a living before slamming was cool. Farm-strong, faith-strong, and not a fan of trash talk.
Heavyweight boxer with a permanent smile and an overhand right that ended careers. Nicest heavyweight to ever knock you out.
A legend of the old Japanese rings where stomping was legal and knees were a love language. His stare-downs could curdle milk.
Destroyed legs for a living and never once complained about his own knees, which are held together by staples and optimism.
Karate master who drank... a famous morning beverage for health reasons that we will not describe. Front kicks you in the face with a peaceful expression.
Smooth talker, smooth wrestler, smooth transition to broadcasting.
Howls at the crowd, wears a giant chain, and once slammed a man so hard the arena felt it. A legendary practical joker with terrible impulse control.
Won a reality show with a fight so bloody it made the sport mainstream. Writes self-deprecating books. The most relatable champion ever.
Olympic wrestler with the most famous right hand in history. Retired at 46 after nearly winning the belt one last time.
The older brother and the original. Mocked opponents mid-fight, skipped every press event he could, and somehow became a legend for it.
Fought giants his whole career and never once complained. The definition of 'heart over size'.
The original featherweight king. Leg kicks that ended careers and a famous sprint into the crowd after a home win.
Built a gym empire and a hairstyle that has not moved since 2006.
Moves in angles that confused opponents and scientists. Now explains footwork on television for forty-minute stretches.
So technically perfect that his greatest weakness was 'being too small for people to notice'. Streams video games and is better at those too.
Two-division champion turned commentator who will remind you he's a two-division champion during unrelated commercial breaks.
The most successful heavyweight champion in history, who also kept his job as a part-time firefighter, which is the most Ohio thing ever.
Two-division champion widely considered the greatest female fighter ever. Retired on top to raise her family.
Made the sport take women's MMA seriously with an armbar nobody could stop. Then left for movies and pro wrestling.
World champion boxer who pulled off one of the biggest upsets in sports history with a head kick.
Built a career on rivalries and comebacks, including choking out a champion in the last minute of a title fight.
Muay Thai world champion whose name defeated more commentators than opponents. Volume striking, terrifying stare-downs.
Basically invented lying on people and punching them. The sport owes him a royalty check.

fighters.nick: The World's Most Dangerous Man (Sunday Brunch Edition)
fighters.bio: The original 'World's Most Dangerous Man'. Still fights in exhibitions at an age when most people fight with their HOA.
Skinny guy in a gi who beat everyone at the very first tournament and changed martial arts forever.
Has more fights than most promotions. Has the most respectable moustache in combat sports history.
Famous for knocking people out and walking away before they hit the ground. Chin made of volcanic rock.
Won every belt in every promotion on earth, often looking like a different person each time.
Has fought in every decade of the sport's existence and simply refuses to stop.
Got beaten up for two rounds every fight and then submitted you in the third with a smile.
Fastest hands of his era and a spinning heel kick everybody still remembers.
Former high-school math teacher who became champion and stayed exactly that nice.
Ended an all-time great reign, then suffered more misfortune than anyone deserved. Keeps showing up.
Champion, model, and the most strongly opinionated man about other people's training methods.
Fought the bloodiest five-round war in history and then smiled with a split lip. Says nothing. Means everything.
Would fight anyone, anywhere, on two weeks' notice, then go wakeboarding the next morning.
Holds the record for most fight-night bonuses by a man who also works in IT.
The most cardio in human history and the most hair. Literally never stops moving.
Walks out screaming 'YES', trains on mountaintops, and once fought with a cut so bad the doctor needed a doctor.
Ran up the cage and kicked a man in the face. The sport has been trying to recreate it ever since.
Fought with a toothpick in his mouth and won a lot of very close decisions. Nobody knows what happened to the toothpicks.
Philadelphia street fighter who won titles in multiple promotions and refuses to stop throwing hands.
Former champion who has fought everyone in three divisions and is still asking for more.

fighters.nick: Right Leg Hospital, Left Leg Cemetery
fighters.bio: Former police officer and politician whose left head kick had its own obituary section.
So calm he looks like he's sleepwalking. Has beaten everyone, everywhere, while looking mildly inconvenienced.
Never lost in his last 22 fights. Now tells stories about bar fights that may or may not have happened, with sound effects.
Early welterweight champion who built the most feared gym in the Midwest.
The first lightweight champion of the modern era, with a left hand that hit far above its weight.
Wore masks to the ring, fought for 90 minutes straight, and made submission grappling look like improv comedy.
San shou champion whose spinning back kicks were so fast that VCR tapes couldn't keep up.

marquee.archetype: The Face of Women's MMA (First Draft)

fighters.bio: Before anyone took women's MMA seriously, she was on magazine covers and action movie sets.
